$comment: Forge-neutral CI gate inventory. Both .github/workflows and .gitlab-ci.yml render it, and node scripts/ci/check-pipelines.mjs verifies every configured forge against it. Add a gate here first, then wire it into every forge; a forge that cannot run a gate must say so with `forges` plus `reason`. See docs/ci-lanes.md.

supplyChain.requirement: The images built are selected by the shared plan from the installed product closure, not enumerated per forge.
Images are produced only by the generated Bake plan, so every image shares one build definition.
Every image carries max-mode BuildKit provenance and an SBOM attestation.
Post-build steps address images by the digest the build reported, never by a mutable tag.
An SPDX SBOM is generated for every published digest.
A CRITICAL or HIGH finding fails the release rather than warning.
Every published digest is signed with keyless cosign against the forge OIDC identity.
The SBOM is attached to the digest as a verifiable SPDX attestation.
SLSA provenance naming the exact source commit is attached to the digest.
The scan result and its severity policy are attached to the digest.
A release is cut from the exact source revision the pipeline verified, never from a branch tip re-resolved at build time.
The release stage follows the reports fan-in and has no needs override that bypasses earlier quality stages.
supplyChain.reason: GitLab enforces the reports fan-in before its release stage; GitHub verifies a completed CI workflow instead of using GitLab stage names.

supplyChain.requirement: GitHub publishes only from the exact revision of a successful push-to-main CI workflow.
supplyChain.reason: GitHub release provenance follows its completed CI workflow; GitLab performs release in the same staged pipeline.

supplyChain.requirement: The current default-branch head is re-read from the remote before a release is published, so a revision it has already moved past is refused.
